newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium renews call for permanent crimes court.
newsitem.headline: Belgium renews call for permanent crimes court.

text.p: Belgium renewed calls on Wednesday to set up a permanent criminal court to improve the handling of major international crimes and streamline criminal jurisprudence.

"We believe this new international jurisdiction would be an extremely suitable instrument for ending the unpunishable status of perpetrators of the most abominable international crimes," Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said.
"This preventive and dissuasive instrument would also guarantee stability and coherence of international criminal jurisprudence," he told a Red Cross colloquium on war crimes.

He added the project, proposed several times in the past but thwarted each time, would be complex as it implied adjusting the sovereignty of states and balancing out powers and responsibilities of states and the court.
Currently, two international war crimes tribunals have been set up on an ad-hoc basis -- one for war crimes committed in ex-Yugoslavia and one for the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.
